Strawberry Nutella Brownies 🍓🤎 Perfect brownies for summer!  (recipe makes an 8x8 pan) Ingredients:  10 tbsp (140g) unsalted butter, melted 1 cup (200g) granulated sugar ¼ cup (50g) brown sugar, packed  2 eggs, room temp 1 tsp vanilla extract ½ cup + 2 tbsp (56g) unsweetened cocoa powder ½ tsp salt 1 tbsp (13g) vegetable oil ½ cup (63g) all purpose flour, spooned & leveled or weighed (don’t pack it in) ¾ cup chocolate chips 190g (~⅔ cup) Nutella  Topping: Strawberry slices, patted dry (as many as you want/enough to cover the top) Nutella (to spread over the top & drizzle)  Instructions: Line an 8x8 pan with parchment paper. Spread the nutella onto the parchment into a thin, even square the size of the pan. Freeze for at least 30 minutes or until frozen solid. Preheat oven to 325°F and line/grease an 8x8 pan with parchment. In a large bowl, whisk melted butter, granulated sugar, and brown sugar until smooth. Add eggs and vanilla, then whisk vigorously for 1-2 minutes. Stir in cocoa powder and salt until fully combined. Mix in oil, then gently fold in the flour until just combined (don’t over mix). Fold in chocolate chips. Spread half the batter into the greased pan. Place the frozen nutella sheet on top of it. Then, spread the remaining batter over it to cover the nutella layer completely. Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until a toothpick near the center comes out with no wet batter. It should just come out with a little nutella & slightly moist crumbs. Let the brownies cool completely. Spread a thin layer of nutella over the cooled brownies, add strawberry slices (patted dry) all over the top, and drizzle with more nutella.  Best enjoyed fresh!  #bakingrecipe #brownies #chocolatestrawberries #nutella #recipe

For the Chicken:  -2 large chicken breasts, flattened  -Seasoning: 1 tbsp paprika, 2 tsp garlic powder, 2 tsp onion powder, 2 tsp Italian seasoning, 2 tsp salt, 2 tsp black pepper, 1–2 tsp cayenne pepper (optional)  -1 tbsp olive oil For the Pasta & Sauce:  -8 oz (225 g) rigatoni  -3 tbsp butter  -1 large shallot, finely diced  -6–8 garlic cloves, minced  -1 cup heavy cream, room temperature  -Seasoning: 1 tsp chicken bouillon powder, 1 tsp paprika, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp Italian seasoning, 1 tsp black pepper  -3/4 cup freshly grated Parmesan (please use fresh!)  -1/2 cup pasta water, as needed (aka liquid gold) Instructions: 1. Slow Cooker Pineapple BBQ Beef Roast Ingredients 1. Beef Chuck Roast – 3–4 lb (1.4–1.8 kg) 2. Pineapple Rings – 1 can (20 oz/565 g), drained, reserving 1/2 cup juice 3. Barbecue Sauce – 1 1/2 cups 4. Pineapple Juice – 1/2 cup, reserved from the can 5. Beef Broth – 1/2 cup 6. Yellow Onion – 1 large, sliced 7. Garlic – 5 cloves, minced 8. Worcestershire Sauce – 2 tbsp 9. Soy Sauce – 2 tbsp 10. Brown Sugar – 2 tbsp 11. Dijon Mustard – 1 tbsp 12. Smoked Paprika – 1 tsp 13. Ground Black Pepper – 1 tsp 14. Salt – 1 tsp, or to taste 15. Onion Powder – 1 tsp 16. Garlic Powder – 1 tsp 17. Olive Oil – 1 tbsp 18. Apple Cider Vinegar – 1 tbsp 19. Cornstarch – 1 tbsp, optional for thickening 20. Cold Water – 2 tbsp, optional for thickening 21. Fresh Parsley – 2 tbsp, chopped, for garnish Recipe 1. Pat the beef chuck roast dry with paper towels. Trim away any unusually thick pieces of excess fat while leaving enough marbling to keep the meat tender during slow cooking. 2. In a small bowl, combine the salt, black pepper, smoked paprika, onion powder, and garlic powder. Rub the seasoning mixture over all sides of the roast so the beef is evenly flavored. 3. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the roast for 3–4 minutes per side until a deep brown crust forms. This step develops extra flavor, although you can skip it when short on time. 4. Place the sliced onion and minced garlic in the bottom of a 6–8-quart slow cooker. Set the seared beef roast on top of the onion mixture. 5. In a medium bowl, whisk together the barbecue sauce, reserved pineapple juice, beef broth, Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce, brown sugar, Dijon mustard, and apple cider vinegar until smooth. 6. Pour the prepared sauce over the beef, coating the top and sides generously. Arrange the pineapple rings around and on top of the roast so their sweet juices mingle with the savory barbecue sauce. 7. Cover the slow cooker with its lid and cook on LOW for 8–10 hours or on HIGH for approximately 4–6 hours, until the beef is fork-tender and pulls apart easily. Cooking time depends on the roast's size and the slow cooker. 8. Halfway through cooking, carefully spoon some of the sauce over the roast if convenient. Keep the lid closed as much as possible so the slow cooker maintains its temperature. 9. Once the beef is tender, transfer it carefully to a large platter. Use two forks to pull it into thick chunks or slices, depending on your preferred presentation. Remove any large pieces of fat. 10. Taste the cooking liquid and adjust the seasoning if necessary. For a richer glaze, transfer approximately 2 cups of the liquid to a saucepan and simmer over medium heat for 8–12 minutes until reduced and glossy. 11. For a thicker sauce, whisk the cornstarch and cold water together in a small bowl until smooth. Stir the slurry into the simmering sauce and cook for 1–2 minutes until thickened. Add only as much as needed to achieve your preferred consistency. 12. Return the beef to the slow cooker or place it in the saucepan with the reduced sauce. Gently toss the meat so every piece is coated in the sweet, tangy pineapple barbecue glaze. 13. Arrange the pineapple rings around the beef on a serving platter. Spoon additional sauce over the roast and garnish with freshly chopped parsley for a colorful finish. 14. Serve the hot pineapple BBQ beef with mashed potatoes, steamed rice, roasted vegetables, or toasted rolls. Spoon extra sauce over each portion and enjoy the tender beef with its smoky, sweet, and savory flavors. Follow for more delicious slow cooker recipes and amazing food ideas!

RESTORATION STEW ✨  A nourishing beef stew made with your period in mind. This rich ginger-braised beef stew combines iron-rich beef and lentils, sweet potato, spinach, ginger, pumpkin seeds and vitamin C-rich red pepper and lemon. And because nourishment should still be delicious, there’s red wine, white miso and a little dark chocolate for serious depth. Save this one for the next time your body is asking for a little extra care. 🥩 BEEF • 1½ lb (680g) cubed chuck roast • 1 lb (454g) cubed boneless short rib • 1½ tsp kosher salt • ¾ tsp black pepper • 2 tbsp olive oil 🥣 STEW • 8 oz (227g) sliced cremini mushrooms • 1 yellow onion, diced • 1 red bell pepper, diced • 5 garlic cloves, minced • 2 tbsp grated ginger • 2 tbsp tomato paste • 1 tsp turmeric • ½ tsp smoked paprika • ½ cup (120ml) dry red wine • 6 cups (1.4L) low-sodium beef stock • 3 thyme sprigs • 1 large sweet potato, cubed • ¾ cup (145g) red lentils, rinsed • 1 tbsp (18g) white/shiro miso • ¾ oz (21g) 70–85% dark chocolate • 3 cups (90g) baby spinach • 1–2 tbsp lemon juice FINISH • ⅓ cup (45g) roasted pumpkin seeds • ¼ cup (15g) parsley • Olive oil + lemon DIRECTIONS 	1	Season beef. Heat oil in a Dutch oven and brown beef in batches. Remove. 	2	Brown mushrooms 4–5 min. Add onion + pepper; cook 4–5 min. Add garlic + ginger; cook 1 min. 	3	Stir in tomato paste, turmeric + paprika; cook 1–2 min. Add wine, scrape up those good brown bits and reduce 2–3 min. 	4	Return beef. Add stock + thyme. Cover and gently simmer 1½–2 hrs until tender. 	5	Remove thyme. Add sweet potato + lentils. Simmer uncovered 20–25 min until tender. Add more stock if needed. 	6	Whisk miso with ½ cup hot broth; stir into stew. Add chocolate and stir until melted. 	7	Add spinach until wilted. Turn off heat and add lemon. Season to taste. Serve with pumpkin seeds, parsley, olive oil + lemon. videos.caption: Bacon Wrapped Carrots with a Maple Dijon Glaze 🥕🥓 the side dish you need to add to your Thanksgiving menu this year! The key step is to roast them on a wire rack so the bacon gets super crispy all around and anything that burns drips onto the aluminum foil for easy cleanup. These are absolutely delicious!  Search ‘crowded kitchen bacon wrapped carrots’ online for the full recipe or head straight here: https://www.crowdedkitchen.com/bacon-wrapped-carrots/ 10 medium carrots about 8 inches long, peeled 10 slices regular-cut bacon Glaze:  3 tablespoons pure maple syrup 2 tablespoons honey 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard 1 tablespoon olive oil ½ teaspoon kosher salt ½ teaspoon smoked paprika ¼ teaspoon dried thyme ¼ teaspoon black pepper 1 teaspoon apple cider vinegar Preheat the oven to 400˚F/200˚C. Set a wire rack over an aluminum foil-lined sheet pan. To a large pot of boiling water, add the whole carrots and blanch for 6 to 7 minutes (about 4 for thin carrots, 8 to 9 for extra-thick ones). Drain and pat completely dry. Starting at the thick end of the carrot, wrap one slice of bacon around each carrot in a spiral. Space the turns so a stripe of carrot shows between each one, with no overlap. At each end, push a toothpick all the way through the bacon and the carrot so it comes out through the bacon on the other side. Lay the carrots on the rack. Place the carrots in the oven for 10, until the fat in the bacon starts to render. Meanwhile, whisk together the maple syrup, honey, Dijon, olive oil, kosher salt, smoked paprika, thyme, black pepper and apple cider vinegar until well combined. Brush the top side of the carrots with about ⅓ of the glaze, then return to the oven and cook another 10-12 minutes. Flip the carrots, brush the side now facing up with another ⅓ of the glaze, and return to the oven for another 10-12 minutes. Flip again, brush with the remaining glaze, and cook a final 10-12 minutes, until the bacon is crisp and the glaze is glossy and set. Test for doneness by sliding a paring knife into the thickest part of a carrot. If it goes in easily, they're done. If not, return them to the oven for 5 more minutes, laying a sheet of foil loosely over the top if the bacon is already crisp. Let rest for 5 minutes so the glaze can set, then remove the toothpicks and finish with herbs. Don't leave the carrots on the wire rack for more than 5 to 10 minutes, or the glaze can make them hard to remove.

Ingredients: •1 Pound Flank Steak, sliced into thin strips •1 Red Bell Pepper, chopped •1 Green Bell Pepper, chopped •1 Medium Yellow Onion, chopped •Pinch of Salt, for vegetables •2 Tablespoons Avocado Oil, or neutral oil of choice, to cook steak & vegetables Steak Marinade: • 2 Tablespoons Low-Sodium Soy Sauce • 4 Cloves Garlic, minced • 1 Tablespoon Avocado Oil, or neutral cooking oil of choice • 2 Teaspoons reduced-sodium Rice Vinegar •1½ Teaspoons Cornstarch •½ Teaspoon Black Pepper •½ Teaspoon Granulated White sugar, or brown sugar •½ Teaspoon Baking Soda Sauce: •½ Cup Low-Sodium Soy Sauce •2 Tablespoons Beef Stock, or unsalted beef stock •2 Tablespoons reduced-sodium Rice Vinegar •1½ Tablespoon Granulated White Sugar, or brown sugar •2 Teaspoons Cornstarch •¼ Teaspoon Black Pepper •(optional) 2 Tablespoons of water, to dilute if too salty for your taste Instructions: 1. Pat steak dry. Thinly slice flank steak against the grain into about ¼-inch strips. Add steak into a medium-sized bowl. 2. For the steak marinade, toss the steak in soy sauce, minced garlic, oil, rice vinegar, cornstarch, black pepper, sugar, and baking soda. Mix well and fully coat the steak in the marinade. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 15 minutes, up to 1 hour. 3. To make the sauce, in a separate medium-sized bowl add in soy sauce, beef stock, rice vinegar, sugar, cornstarch, and black pepper. Mix and whisk together ingredients well. Set aside. 4. When ready to cook, heat a large skillet to medium-high heat. Add in 2 tbsp cooking oil. Once oil is hot, shimmers and easily moves around the skillet, add steak to the skillet in batches. Be sure not to overcrowd the skillet. Sear steak for about 1 minute to brown and then flip over to continue cooking for an additional 1 minute to brown. Remove from the skillet and repeat until all of the steak is cooked. 5. Once done cooking the steak, reduce heat to medium, add in more oil if necessary, then toss in chopped onion and chopped bell peppers. Sprinkle with a pinch of salt and saute for a couple of minutes until onions and peppers are slightly softened. 6. Next, pour the sauce into the skillet, stir and simmer for a few minutes until the sauce thickens. Then, toss the steak into the skillet and mix well until all ingredients are combined and the steak is reheated. Serve and enjoy.

Chocolate Chip Cookies 🍪 (Makes 9-10 Cookies)  Ingredients: - 1/2 cup (115g) unsalted butter, melted and cooled - 1/2 cup (100g) light brown sugar - 1/3 cup (67g) granulated sugar - 1 large egg, room temp - 1 tablespoon (15g) vanilla extract - 1 1/4 cups (160g) all-purpose flour, spooned and leveled - 1/2 teaspoon (2g) baking soda - Pinch of salt - 1 1/2 cups (190g) semi-sweet chocolate chips For Garnish: - Flaky sea salt ( optional ) Method: 1. Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. 2. In a bowl, whisk together flour, baking soda, and salt. Set aside. 3. In a separate bowl, combine melted butter, brown sugar, and granulated sugar. Whisk for 1-2 minutes until a smooth paste forms. 4. Crack in the egg and vanilla extract. Mix until well combined. 5. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet batter and gently fold until just combined. 6. Add chocolate chips and mix with a spatula. Do not overmix the batter. 7. Scoop out 9 cookies onto the prepared baking sheet, leaving about 2 inches of space between each cookie. 8. Bake for 12 minutes or until golden brown and crispy on the edges and gooey in the center. 9. Remove from the oven and sprinkle with flaky sea salt. 10. The secret to making this lemony chickpea orzo soup creamy isn’t dairy—you actually get that creaminess from pureeing a bit of the soup with some tahini. Lemony Chickpea Orzo Soup Recipe Makes 6 servings INGREDIENTS 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil 1 large yellow onion, chopped 2 medium carrots, peeled and sliced 4 stalks celery, thinly sliced 3 garlic cloves, minced 1 teaspoon dried thyme 2 quarts (8 cups) lower-sodium vegetable broth  2 (15.5-oz.) cans chickpeas, rinsed and drained 3/4 cup dry orzo pasta (regular or whole-wheat) 2 tablespoons tahini 3 handfuls roughly chopped or shredded kale (sub spinach, Swiss Chard, or escarole) 1-2 lemons (depends how juicy they are) 2 Tbsp. finely chopped fresh dill, plus more for garnish DIRECTIONS Heat oil in a large stock pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Once hot, add the onion, carrots, and celery. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened. Add garlic and thyme; cook 1 more minute, until aromatic. Add broth and increase heat to bring mixture to a boil. Once boiling, add chickpeas and the orzo. Simmer soup over medium-high heat, uncovered, for 10 minutes, or until the orzo is al dente. Reduce heat to low. Remove about 1 1/2 cups of soup and add to a blender with the tahini. Puree until smooth then pour back into the pot. (Or use an immersion blender to partially puree the soup.) Add kale and continue to cook over low heat for 5 minutes, or until greens are wilted.  Stir in juice and zest from 1 lemon (taste and add more from second lemon if needed), fresh dill and taste/adjust seasonings as needed. Ladle soup into bowls and garnish with extra fresh dill, cracked black pepper, and a drizzle of olive oil, if desired

🔥 SAVE THIS RECIPE! 🥩🍚 CREAMY KOREAN BEEF BULGOGI RICE BOWL! Juicy, caramelized beef coated in a rich, creamy Korean-inspired sauce, served over fluffy white rice! 🤤🔥 Sweet, savory, garlicky, and just the right amount of heat. This is the kind of dinner you'll want on repeat! 🛒 INGREDIENTS (Serves 3–4) 🥩 For the beef: 1 lb thinly sliced ribeye or sirloin steak 3 tbsp soy sauce 1 tbsp brown sugar 1 tbsp sesame oil 3 cloves garlic, minced 1 tsp fresh grated ginger 1 tbsp rice vinegar ½ tsp black pepper 1 tbsp neutral cooking oil 🥣 For the creamy Korean sauce: 3 tbsp mayonnaise 2 tbsp sour cream 1 tbsp gochujang (Korean chili paste) 1 tsp soy sauce 1 tsp honey 1 tsp lime juice 1–2 tbsp water to adjust consistency 🍚 For serving: 3 cups cooked jasmine rice 2 green onions, chopped 1 tsp sesame seeds Optional: chili flakes or extra sauce 👩‍🍳 HOW TO MAKE IT 1️⃣ Marinate the beef: Mix soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, rice vinegar, and black pepper. Toss with the sliced beef and marinate for 20–30 minutes in the refrigerator. 2️⃣ Make the creamy sauce: Whisk together mayonnaise, sour cream, gochujang, soy sauce, honey, and lime juice. Add a little water until smooth and creamy. 3️⃣ Sear the beef: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook beef in batches for 2–4 minutes, turning until beautifully browned and cooked through. 4️⃣ Get it saucy: Reduce heat to low. Add a few spoonfuls of creamy Korean sauce and gently toss the beef until coated. 5️⃣ Build your bowl: Spoon fluffy jasmine rice into serving bowls and pile the juicy bulgogi beef on top. 6️⃣ Finish: Drizzle with extra creamy sauce, then sprinkle with fresh green onions and sesame seeds. ✨ PRO TIP: Cook the beef in batches! Overcrowding the pan causes steaming instead of that delicious caramelized sear. 🔥 NOW BE HONEST!
